_metadata.title: Indian Nutrition Knowledge Base
_metadata.description: Comprehensive nutrition knowledge base for an Indian audience health app, covering ICMR guidelines, food composition data, regional diet patterns, health-goal-specific nutrition, food synergies, and glycemic indices.
primary_sources: ICMR-NIN Recommended Dietary Allowances for Indians (2020, updated 2024)
Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT 2017), NIN Hyderabad
Nutritive Value of Indian Foods (NVIF), NIN Hyderabad
Longvah T et al., Indian Food Composition Tables, NIN, 2017
ICMR-NIN Expert Group on Nutrient Requirements (2020)
Foster-Powell K et al., International Tables of Glycemic Index, Am J Clin Nutr, 2002
Atkinson FS et al., International Tables of GI and GL Values, Diabetes Care, 2008
Radhika G et al., Glycaemic index of Indian foods, Br J Nutr, 2010
NIN. My Plate for the Day - Guidelines, 2024
WHO/FAO Expert Consultation on Diet, Nutrition and Prevention of Chronic Diseases, 2003
_metadata.disclaimer: Values are approximate and based on published ICMR-NIN, IFCT 2017, and peer-reviewed data. Actual nutrient content may vary by cultivar, region, cooking method, and season. This data is for educational and app reference purposes; it does not substitute for professional medical or dietary advice.

section_1_icmr_dietary_guidelines.title: ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians (2024)
section_1_icmr_dietary_guidelines.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research - National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN) published updated dietary guidelines in 2024, revising earlier 2011 guidelines. Key changes include increased protein recommendations, updated fat quality guidance, emphasis on millets, and specific guidance on ultra-processed food avoidance.
key_principles: Eat a variety of foods to ensure a balanced diet
Ensure adequacy of cereals, millets, pulses in every meal
Consume at least 400g of vegetables and fruits daily
Use oils and fats in moderation; choose variety of cooking oils
Limit intake of salt to less than 5g per day
Limit consumption of sugar and ultra-processed foods
Adopt a healthy lifestyle with adequate physical activity
Drink adequate water (8-10 glasses per day)
Promote exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months
Include millets as part of the daily diet

recommended_dietary_allowances_rda.description: RDA values as per ICMR-NIN 2020 (latest revision with 2024 updates)

energy_requirements_kcal_per_day.reference: ICMR-NIN Expert Group Report on Nutrient Requirements, 2020

protein_g_per_day.description: Based on 0.83 g/kg/day for adults (revised upward from 1 g/kg for Indian diets due to lower digestibility of plant-based protein; effective recommendation ~1.0-1.2 g/kg for mixed Indian diet)

adults.note: For Indian mixed vegetarian diet, increase by 20% to account for lower digestibility: men ~65g, women ~55g

fat_g_per_day.description: Visible fat (cooking oil + butter/ghee); total fat should provide 20-30% of energy

carbohydrates.note: Emphasis on complex carbs; limit free sugars to <10% energy (ideally <5%)

protein.note: Higher end for vegetarians; at least 1/3 from pulses/legumes

fat.note: Not below 20% to ensure essential fatty acid adequacy

fiber.note: From whole grains, vegetables, fruits, pulses

vitamin_d_iu.note: ICMR recommends 400-600 IU; many Indians are deficient

vitamin_b12_mcg.note: Critical for vegetarians; supplement if needed

my_plate_for_the_day_icmr.description: ICMR-NIN recommended plate composition per meal and daily portions

vegetables.note: Include leafy greens daily, at least 50g

section_3_regional_diet_patterns.title: Regional Indian Diet Patterns
section_3_regional_diet_patterns.description: India has distinct regional dietary cultures shaped by climate, agriculture, religion, and tradition. Understanding these is critical for personalized nutrition recommendations.

north_indian.region: Punjab, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan, Delhi, HP, J&K, Uttarakhand

typical_meal_pattern.breakfast: Paratha with curd/pickle, or Poha/Upma, Tea with milk
typical_meal_pattern.lunch: 2-3 Rotis, 1 dal, 1 sabzi (vegetable), rice, salad (onion-cucumber), curd
typical_meal_pattern.dinner: Similar to lunch, sometimes lighter - khichdi or roti-sabzi

nutritional_strengths: High protein from generous dairy and pulses
Wheat provides more protein than rice
nutritional_concerns: Low vegetable diversity in some households

seasonal_foods.winter: Sarson saag, Gajar halwa, Mooli paratha, Bajra roti, Gur (jaggery), Rewri-Gajak
seasonal_foods.summer: Lassi, Aam Panna, Shikanji, Raita, Sattu drink, Watermelon

south_indian.region: Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana

typical_meal_pattern.breakfast: Idli/Dosa/Pongal with sambar and coconut chutney, Filter coffee
typical_meal_pattern.lunch: Rice + Sambar + Rasam + Vegetable poriyal + Curd + Pickle + Papadum (Thali format, banana leaf)
typical_meal_pattern.dinner: Lighter - idli/dosa or rice with rasam/curd

nutritional_strengths: Fermented foods (idli/dosa) improve B12 and mineral bioavailability
Coconut provides MCTs and lauric acid
nutritional_concerns: Can be low in protein if dal portions are small
Excess coconut oil in some preparations

seasonal_foods.summer: Neer Mor (spiced buttermilk), Panagam, Raw mango rice, Tender coconut water

east_indian.region: West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand, Assam, Northeast states
primary_proteins: Fish (Hilsa, Rohu, Katla - Bengal, Assam, Odisha are major fish-eating regions)

typical_meal_pattern.breakfast: Luchi/Paratha or Muri (puffed rice) with tea, or Sattu drink (Bihar)
typical_meal_pattern.lunch: Rice (generous portion) + Dal + Fish/Egg curry + Sabzi + Chutney (tomato/raw mango)
typical_meal_pattern.dinner: Rice + lighter fish preparation or dal-sabzi

nutritional_strengths: Excellent omega-3 from fish and mustard oil
nutritional_concerns: Low vegetable variety in some areas
unique_superfoods: Sattu (roasted Bengal gram flour): 20g protein per 100g, cooling, sustained energy
Bamboo shoots (NE): Low calorie, high fiber, antioxidants

typical_meal_pattern.lunch: Bhakri (jowar/bajra) or Roti/Rice + Dal + Sabzi + Koshimbir (salad) + Loncha (pickle) + Papad + (Goa: Fish curry rice)

nutritional_strengths: Millets (jowar, bajra) as staples - higher protein, fiber, minerals than rice
Kokum/Sol Kadhi - rich in hydroxycitric acid, antioxidants
nutritional_concerns: Gujarat diet can be high in sugar (jaggery/sugar in savory dishes)
Deep fried snacks common (fafda, vada pav, bhajiya)
Goan diet can be high in coconut cream and alcohol

section_4_nutrition_for_health_goals.title: Research-Backed Nutrition for Specific Health Goals

fat_loss_and_cholesterol_reduction.goal: Reduce body fat percentage and improve lipid profile (lower LDL, triglycerides; raise HDL)
key_principles: Caloric deficit of 300-500 kcal/day for sustainable fat loss (0.5-1 kg/week)
High protein (1.2-1.6 g/kg) to preserve lean mass during deficit
High fiber (30-40g/day) for satiety and cholesterol binding
Reduce refined carbs and added sugars
Include soluble fiber sources to lower LDL cholesterol
Choose MUFA/PUFA-rich fats over saturated fats

top_foods.reason: Beta-glucan soluble fiber lowers LDL by 5-10%; high satiety
High protein + fiber; low GI; pulses reduce LDL
Galactomannan fiber binds cholesterol; reduces triglycerides
ALA omega-3 + lignans; reduces total and LDL cholesterol
Soluble fiber binds bile acids; high satiety protein
Beta-glucan even higher than oats; powerful LDL reducer
Very low calorie, high volume, fiber, micronutrients
MUFA + fiber; reduces LDL without weight gain (if portion controlled)
Allicin reduces total cholesterol 10-12% in studies
Comparable to statins in some studies for LDL reduction; 1 amla or amla juice daily
Curcumin reduces inflammatory markers; modest LDL reduction
Enhanced protein, reduced antinutrients, very low calorie
Probiotics, low calorie, replaces high-cal lassi
Higher fiber and protein than rice; lower GI

foods_to_limit: Refined flour (maida) products - naan, bhature, biscuits, white bread
Deep fried snacks - samosa, pakora, puri
Sugar - mithai, sweetened beverages, added sugar in chai
Excess ghee/butter (>2 tsp/day during fat loss)
White rice in large portions (switch to brown rice or millets)
Trans fats - vanaspati, margarine, bakery products

references: Bazzano LA et al., Non-soy legume consumption lowers cholesterol: meta-analysis, Nutr Metab Cardiovasc Dis, 2011
Ried K et al., Garlic for cardiovascular risk reduction, Cochrane Database, 2012
Pan A et al., Alpha-linolenic acid and cardiovascular outcomes, Am J Clin Nutr, 2012
Khosla P et al., Amla (Emblica officinalis) and lipid lowering, Eur J Clin Nutr, 2011

muscle_building.goal: Increase lean muscle mass and strength through optimal nutrition
key_principles: Caloric surplus of 300-500 kcal/day above maintenance
Protein: 1.6-2.2 g/kg body weight (ISSN recommendation)
Distribute protein across 4-5 meals (30-40g per meal for maximal MPS)
Combine plant proteins for complete amino acid profile
Adequate leucine (2.5-3g per meal) to trigger muscle protein synthesis
Carbs: 4-7 g/kg for glycogen replenishment and training fuel
Creatine monohydrate (3-5g/day) - most evidence-backed supplement

section_5_indian_food_combinations.title: Indian Food Combinations for Optimal Nutrition (Food Synergies)
section_5_indian_food_combinations.description: Traditional Indian food pairings often have scientific rationale for enhanced nutrient absorption and complete nutrition. These ancestral food wisdoms are now being validated by modern nutrition science.

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Rice is deficient in lysine but rich in methionine. Legumes are rich in lysine but deficient in methionine. Together they form a complete protein with all essential amino acids, approaching the quality of animal protein (amino acid complementation).
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Staple combination across all of India (Rajma-Chawal, Dal-Chawal, Sambar-Rice, Dal-Bhaat)
references: Young VR & Pellett PL, Am J Clin Nutr, 1994 - Plant protein complementation

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Piperine in black pepper inhibits glucuronidation of curcumin in the liver, increasing curcumin bioavailability by 2000%. Fat (oil/ghee) further enhances absorption since curcumin is lipophilic. This triple combination is found naturally in many Indian curries.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Every Indian curry contains this combination: turmeric + black pepper in an oil/ghee base
synergistic_combinations.optimal_ratio: 1/4 tsp turmeric + pinch of black pepper + 1 tsp oil/ghee
references: Shoba G et al., Influence of Piperine on the Pharmacokinetics of Curcumin, Planta Med, 1998

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Non-heme iron (plant-based) absorption is only 2-5%. Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) converts ferric iron (Fe3+) to ferrous iron (Fe2+), increasing absorption by 3-6 fold. This is critical for vegetarian Indians who rely on plant iron.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Squeezing lemon on dal, salad with meals, amla pickle/chutney with food, lemon on sprouts
examples: Amla chutney with iron-rich ragi roti
Lemon juice on sprouted moong (high iron + high C)
Tomato-based curry with leafy greens (tomato provides C)
references: Hallberg L et al., Effect of ascorbic acid on iron absorption, Am J Clin Nutr, 1989

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Curd provides probiotics (Lactobacillus) that improve gut health and mineral absorption. Lactic acid in curd enhances calcium and iron absorption from the meal. The combination also provides complete protein (cereal + dairy).
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Curd rice (Thayir Sadam in South India), Roti with dahi, Raita with biryani
synergistic_combinations.additional_benefit: Probiotics in curd break down phytates in cereals, releasing bound minerals

synergistic_combinations.combination: Fat-soluble Vitamins (A, D, E, K) + Fat/Oil
synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Vitamins A, D, E, K are fat-soluble and require dietary fat for absorption. Cooking vegetables in oil or adding ghee dramatically increases carotenoid (provitamin A) absorption - up to 6x for beta-carotene.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Indian sabzi is always cooked with oil/ghee tadka; carrots in gajar halwa (with ghee); palak paneer (fat from paneer and oil)
examples: Palak cooked with oil/ghee (enhances Vitamin A/K absorption)
Tadka on dal with ghee (enhances vitamin absorption)
Tomato cooked in oil (lycopene becomes 4x more bioavailable)
references: Brown MJ et al., Carotenoid bioavailability with fat, Am J Clin Nutr, 2004

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Jaggery is rich in iron (11mg/100g). Sesame provides iron (14.6mg) + calcium (975mg). Together they provide a significant dose of both minerals. Jaggery's natural sugars aid sesame mineral absorption.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Til-Gur laddoo eaten during Makar Sankranti / winter - provides warmth and minerals during cold months
synergistic_combinations.additional_benefit: Sesame lignans (sesamin) have synergistic anti-inflammatory effects

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Fermentation by Leuconostoc mesenteroides and Lactobacillus (1) creates amino acid complementation between rice and urad dal, (2) increases B-vitamin content (especially B12 - rare in vegetarian foods), (3) reduces phytic acid by 50-60% increasing mineral bioavailability, (4) produces probiotics.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: South Indian staple breakfast; the fermentation process is the key nutritional enhancer
references: Reddy NR et al., Fermentation of cereals and legumes, CRC Critical Reviews in Food Science, 1982

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Legumes are high in non-heme iron but also high in phytates (which inhibit iron absorption). Onion and garlic (sulfur compounds) + Vitamin C from tomato and lemon counteract phytates and enhance iron absorption by 50-70%.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Standard preparation method: Rajma/Chole curry with onion-tomato base, served with lemon wedge and onion rings
references: Gautam S et al., Higher bio-accessibility of iron from cysteine-rich foods, J Nutr, 2010

synergistic_combinations.combination: Tea/Coffee consumed SEPARATELY from iron-rich meals
synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Tannins in tea and polyphenols in coffee reduce non-heme iron absorption by 50-90%. Maintaining a 1-hour gap between iron-rich meals and tea/coffee dramatically improves iron status.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Indians often drink chai immediately after meals - this is nutritionally counterproductive for iron absorption
synergistic_combinations.recommendation: Wait at least 1 hour after meals before drinking tea/coffee; or drink between meals

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Coconut milk/oil provides MCTs that rapidly absorb curcumin. The fat in coconut is the delivery vehicle for the lipophilic curcumin. Combined with black pepper (standard in Kerala cuisine), this is a triple absorption enhancer.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Kerala curries and Avial use coconut paste + turmeric + pepper

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Amla's extremely high Vitamin C preserves and enhances curcumin's antioxidant activity. Honey provides osmotic antibacterial effects and enzymes. The combination creates a synergistic antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effect greater than any component alone.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Chyawanprash contains this combination; also common Ayurvedic home remedy

synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption from the gut. Without adequate Vitamin D, only 10-15% of dietary calcium is absorbed. With adequate D, absorption increases to 30-40%.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Ragi (high calcium) consumed by Karnataka farmers who work in sunlight; traditional practice of sun-drying foods
synergistic_combinations.recommendation: Get 15-20 minutes of midday sun on arms/face + consume ragi, sesame, dairy for calcium

synergistic_combinations.combination: Sabja seeds (Basil seeds) / Chia seeds in water/milk
synergistic_combinations.scientific_rationale: The mucilaginous fiber forms a gel that slows gastric emptying, reducing glycemic response of the meal by 30-40%. Also increases satiety. Soaking activates enzymes and reduces antinutrients.
synergistic_combinations.traditional_context: Falooda with sabja seeds; Ayurvedic practice of soaking seeds overnight

combinations_to_avoid.rationale: Citric acid curdles casein in milk, potentially causing digestive discomfort. Ayurveda considers this Viruddha Ahara (incompatible food).
combinations_to_avoid.modern_nuance: Mild curdling does not necessarily harm digestion in all people; yogurt-based drinks with citrus are consumed globally. Individual tolerance varies.

combinations_to_avoid.rationale: Traditional Ayurvedic Viruddha Ahara. The scientific basis is debated; some suggest different digestion rates and potential for allergic reactions. Widely avoided in Indian households.
combinations_to_avoid.modern_nuance: No strong modern evidence of harm; some cuisines combine fish and cream (e.g., Scandinavian). Cultural practice; follow individual tolerance.

combinations_to_avoid.combination: High oxalate foods (spinach, beetroot) as sole calcium source
combinations_to_avoid.rationale: Oxalic acid binds calcium forming insoluble calcium oxalate, reducing calcium absorption to near zero. Spinach has high calcium on paper (99mg/100g) but <5% is bioavailable.
combinations_to_avoid.recommendation: Do not rely on spinach for calcium. Use dairy, ragi, sesame, chia for calcium. Cook high-oxalate greens (blanching reduces oxalate 30-87%).

combinations_to_avoid.rationale: Tannins in tea chelate iron, reducing absorption by 50-90%. This is a major contributor to India's iron deficiency epidemic.
combinations_to_avoid.recommendation: Drink tea at least 1 hour before or after meals; never with iron-rich foods.

section_6_glycemic_index_indian_foods.title: Glycemic Index (GI) of Common Indian Foods
section_6_glycemic_index_indian_foods.description: GI ranks foods 0-100 based on how quickly they raise blood glucose. Low GI (<55), Medium GI (56-69), High GI (70+). GL (Glycemic Load) = GI x carbs per serving / 100. Sources: International Tables of GI (Foster-Powell 2002, Atkinson 2008), Radhika G et al. 2010, and Henry CJ et al.

classification.low_gi: 55 or below - slow, gradual rise in blood sugar
classification.high_gi: 70 or above - rapid spike in blood sugar

cereals_and_grains.note: Low GI but ultra-processed; not recommended

pulses_and_legumes.note: One of the lowest GI foods known

prepared_indian_foods.note: Fermented but high GI due to refined rice
Fermented, steamed - better than fried snacks
Paneer itself is very low GI; depends on gravy

fruits.note: GI increases with ripeness; raw banana GI is much lower (~30)
High GI but very low GL (mostly water)
Low GI but high GL due to sugar density

vegetables.note: Leafy greens, gourds, cruciferous veg all have very low GI
Lower GI than potato; even lower when boiled (54)
Medium GI but very low GL

sweets_and_beverages.note: Same GI as sugar but richer in minerals
Besan (chickpea flour) base keeps GI lower

tips_to_lower_glycemic_response: Eat protein and fat before carbs in a meal (reduces glucose spike by 30-40%)
Add vinegar/lemon to meals (acetic acid slows starch digestion)
Cook and cool rice/potato (increases resistant starch, lowers GI by 10-15 points)
Replace white rice with brown rice, millets, or mix dal into rice
Add fenugreek (methi) seeds to flour or soak and eat before meals
Walk for 10-15 minutes after meals (GLUT4 translocation clears glucose)
Eat whole fruits instead of fruit juice (fiber slows sugar absorption)
Include cinnamon in meals/drinks (improves insulin sensitivity)
Pair high-GI foods with low-GI foods (e.g., rice + dal, idli + sambar)
Choose desi (Indian) chana varieties over kabuli for lower GI
Apple cider vinegar (1 tbsp in water before meals) reduces postprandial glucose
references: Foster-Powell K et al., International Tables of Glycemic Index and Glycemic Load Values, Am J Clin Nutr, 2002
Atkinson FS et al., International Tables of GI and GL Values: 2008, Diabetes Care, 2008
Radhika G et al., Glycaemic index of Indian flatbreads and rice preparations, Br J Nutr, 2010
Henry CJK et al., Glycaemic index of common foods in South Asian countries, Nutr Res Rev, 2008
Shobana S et al., Glycaemic index of Indian meals, Br J Nutr, 2011

indian_superfoods_summary.description: Foods that are exceptionally nutrient-dense, locally available, affordable, and backed by both traditional use and modern science

superfoods.name: Amla (Indian Gooseberry)
superfoods.why: Highest natural Vitamin C source (600mg/100g); powerful antioxidant; cholesterol reducer; hair tonic; skin brightener; immune booster. Comparable to Acai/Blueberry at fraction of cost.

superfoods.name: Moringa (Drumstick leaves)
superfoods.why: 2x protein of yogurt, 4x calcium of milk, 7x Vitamin C of oranges, 4x Vitamin A of carrots, 25x iron of spinach per weight. 'Miracle tree.'

superfoods.name: Turmeric (Haldi)
superfoods.why: Curcumin is the most studied phytocompound globally with 14,000+ studies. Anti-inflammatory comparable to ibuprofen without side effects.

superfoods.name: Ragi (Finger Millet)
superfoods.why: Richest cereal in calcium (344mg/100g). Low GI. Tryptophan for sleep. Iron. Gluten-free. Perfect for growing children and elderly.

superfoods.name: Sattu (Roasted Bengal Gram Flour)
superfoods.why: 20g protein/100g, natural coolant, high fiber, affordable, sustained energy. Bihar's gift to Indian nutrition.

superfoods.name: Ashwagandha
superfoods.why: Most evidence-backed adaptogen. Reduces cortisol 30%, increases testosterone 15-17%, improves sleep, muscle strength, and fertility.

superfoods.name: Jackfruit (raw/unripe)
superfoods.why: Meat substitute for vegetarians (shredded texture mimics meat). High fiber, potassium, Vitamin B6. Sustainable crop.

superfoods.name: Kokum
superfoods.why: Contains Hydroxycitric Acid (HCA) - natural appetite suppressant and fat metabolism enhancer. Antioxidant. Konkan superfood.

superfoods.name: Black sesame seeds (Kala Til)
superfoods.why: 975mg calcium/100g (8x milk per weight). Iron 14.6mg. Lignans for hormone balance. Anti-aging.

superfoods.name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
superfoods.why: Adaptogen, anti-stress, anti-microbial, anti-diabetic. India's most sacred plant is also a potent medicinal herb.

common_indian_nutritional_deficiencies.description: Widespread nutritional deficiencies in the Indian population and food-based solutions

deficiencies.prevalence: Over 50% of Indian women are anemic (NFHS-5, 2019-21)
deficiencies.food_solutions: Bajra, ragi, dates, jaggery, amla (for absorption), green leafy vegetables, sesame seeds. Avoid tea with meals.

deficiencies.prevalence: 70-90% of Indians are deficient despite living in a tropical country (indoor lifestyle, pollution, dark skin)
deficiencies.food_solutions: Sun exposure 15-20 min midday, fortified milk, eggs, fish, mushrooms exposed to UV. Supplement 1000-2000 IU if deficient.

deficiencies.prevalence: 47% of North Indians deficient (high vegetarian population); B12 found only in animal foods
deficiencies.food_solutions: Dairy, eggs, fermented foods (some B12 from bacterial synthesis in idli/dosa batter), fortified foods, nutritional yeast. Vegetarians should supplement.
Ragi (344mg/100g), sesame (975mg), dairy, chia seeds (631mg), moringa leaves, amaranth leaves. Ensure Vitamin D for absorption.

deficiencies.prevalence: 73% of Indians are protein deficient (IMRB survey). Average intake ~50g vs requirement ~55-65g
deficiencies.food_solutions: 2-3 servings dal daily, sprouts, paneer, eggs, soy chunks, sattu, peanuts, milk. Aim for protein in every meal.

deficiencies.prevalence: Widespread subclinical deficiency; phytate-rich diets reduce absorption
deficiencies.food_solutions: Pumpkin seeds, sesame, cashews, chickpeas, mushrooms, wheat germ, sprouting/soaking reduces phytates

deficiencies.prevalence: Very low intake in vegetarian populations; Indian omega-6:omega-3 ratio is 20-50:1 (should be 5-10:1)
deficiencies.food_solutions: Flaxseed (richest plant source), walnuts, chia seeds, mustard oil (has some ALA), fatty fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel)
Whole grains instead of refined, all millets, rajma, whole chana, vegetables with every meal, fruits with skin, flaxseed, chia

oil_rotation_guide.description: ICMR recommends rotating cooking oils to achieve balanced fatty acid profile. No single oil is perfect.

recommended_rotation.benefit: Best n-6:n-3 ratio; covers MUFA + PUFA; traditional and affordable
Oryzanol from rice bran + ALA from mustard; heart-healthy

recommended_rotation.combination: Coconut oil + Groundnut oil + Flaxseed oil (cold)
recommended_rotation.benefit: MCTs + MUFA + Omega-3; South Indian household

recommended_rotation.combination: Ghee (small amount for flavor) + Sesame oil (cooking) + Flaxseed oil (cold)

oil_rotation_guide.daily_oil_limit: 3-4 teaspoons visible fat total (15-20ml) for sedentary adults
oil_rotation_guide.note: ICMR strongly advises against using a single oil for all cooking. Blend or rotate monthly.
